S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is characterized by one or more depressive episodes lasting at least two weeks, during which individuals experience a persistently low or irritable mood and/or markedly diminished interest or pleasure in most activities, accompanied by additional cognitive, physical, or emotional changes that cause significant distress or functional impairment. Typical features include alterations in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, self-worth, and thoughts about death or suicide, but the specific symptom pattern and severity can vary widely across individuals and episodes. The course may be single-episode or recurrent, often emerging in the context of psychosocial stressors but not fully explained by them, and it is distinguished from normal sadness by its pervasiveness, duration, and impact on functioning, as well as from bipolar disorders by the absence of past manic or hypomanic episodes. Accurate diagnosis requires ruling out substance-induced or medical causes and differentiating it from grief reactions and adjustment disorders that are more time-limited or stressor-bound.

patient.stressor: In the months leading up to his presentation, Robert had been pushing himself hard—working as a therapy assistant, leading teen groups, and taking on extra documentation responsibilities at the clinic while also staying up late to practice guitar and keep up with friends. About five weeks before seeking care, a cluster of difficult cases at work and a tense disagreement with a supervising clinician about treatment plans left him questioning his competence and worrying that he was "out of his depth" in mental health work. Over the following month, he became increasingly withdrawn after shifts, spending long nights alone in his apartment ruminating about whether his clients were getting worse because of him and scrolling through social media posts about burnout and failure in helping professions. When he began having intrusive thoughts about not wanting to wake up and drafted a note on his phone after a particularly stressful day at the clinic, he confided in a trusted colleague, who immediately alerted their supervisor and helped arrange an urgent psychiatric evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: Lately I keep thinking my clients would be better off if I just weren’t here, and those thoughts about not wanting to wake up are starting to scare me.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to look forward to my guitar jams and hanging out with the guys after work, but for the past few weeks it all feels pointless, like I’m just going through the motions and would rather sit in the dark staring at nothing than pretend I’m enjoying anything.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: Most days I have to force myself to eat a couple bites of something because I just don’t feel hungry at all, and I’ve noticed my pants are looser and coworkers keep asking if I’m losing weight.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: I lie in bed exhausted but wired, staring at the ceiling for hours replaying sessions in my head, and even when I finally crash I wake up two or three times a night and drag myself out of bed at 5 a.m. feeling like I never actually slept.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: Even on days when I don’t have groups, just getting showered and walking to the clinic feels like I’ve run a marathon, and by the time my first client arrives I’m already completely drained and fighting to stay upright in my chair.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I keep telling myself that I’m a fraud who’s probably making my clients worse, and I replay every little mistake from sessions until I’m convinced I don’t deserve this job or the trust people put in me.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: My brain feels like it’s full of mud—during sessions I lose my train of thought mid-sentence, can’t remember what a client said five minutes ago, and even simple things like choosing what to eat or writing a short progress note can paralyze me for way too long.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: Pretty much every night now I catch myself thinking it would be a relief if I just didn’t wake up, and on my worst day I actually wrote out a note on my phone explaining how my clients would be better off with a different therapist and started looking up ways people kill themselves before I scared myself and reached out to my coworker.
